briefing: The corridor still has four cleaner rectangles where brass was. The chart at the end of it has fourteen rows and no names. A woman you have seen wipe dust into a palm-sized rectangle is standing under it with a pencil on a string. She does not start. She waits. The kettle in the mess clicks off and nobody fetches it. She will not write the first name unless someone says the wall may be used.

stages.text: Print date before the Exchange. Fourteen rows. Occupation, watch, remarks. Remarks were not ruled for jokes. The pencil point is four millimetres. A knife-nick in the rail, one letter wide, aborted. You can steal the pencil. You can leave it.

Who slept here. That's the only column she can fill without lying. She will not write a Blank Rows name. She will not write a person on a stool. She will not write a nickname unless you tell her the nickname is what they answer to. Graphite comes off. That's the point of it.
Pencil morning row, leave the dust, or wait for ink. Ink is a levy. She does not choose ink.

Optional: if the clerk has started, three occupations on his form, each wrong by one. Mason / caretaker. Clerk / clerk-grade. Veterinary assistant / veterinarian. You held the two papers in the same lamp.
Mess. Ladle on its nail. Tell the Stack, or don't. People read walls.

choices.text: Write who slept here. Pencil. The string ticks the rail. She writes three names you can see from here, occupation as observed, watch blank. The graphite shines. She does not look proud. She looks at the kettle.
Leave it. Wipe the dust if you want. Forty days of this is a politics. She will ask again. She will not ask twice in one morning.
Wait. If we write, we write so it doesn't come off. Ink is a levy. She doesn't choose ink. She will wait. The dust will still come. She will still wipe it. Do not take that for agreement.

briefing: Evening. Steam on the enamel. Kess has scratched a line on the rim of the pot: heads, then scoops. The numbers do not match. Either a portion is missing, or two bowls at the far end are covered because three people are north and the cloth is already taking dust. Ansel's child is on the bench, feet not touching the floor. The ladle hangs too high for them. She can pour. She cannot decide. Deciding is why the ladle is on a nail.

stages.text: Heads in the room. Scoops in the pot. Covered bowls if levy honoured. A ring on one bowl from a noon that was not eaten. The arithmetic is public.
Who goes without, who takes extra, or leave the last bowl until it is cold. The ladle is the vote.
Tell the child the truth, a softer sentence, or send them out. Ansel will not ask twice whether you told the truth at the table.
Optional: Kess can write an order on the mess wall, not the duty chart. Child first. Watch first. Sick first. She will not write fair. She will write an order. Different paper. Different crime.

choices.text: The last scoop goes to the child. An adult's bowl is water and salt. Ansel does not thank you. The child looks at the water-bowl and then does not.
The last scoop goes to whoever has the night slate. They eat standing. The child asks why the ladle likes the grille.
The last bowl sits until it is cold. Nobody takes it. The ring it leaves is brown and stays.
She pencils an order on the mess wall, not the duty chart. Child first, or watch first, or sick first. She will not write fair.

briefing: Intercom. Cracked button. Tamsin: 'Say again. I have a wind. There's a person on the apron. They want a bunk. Manifest says fourteen. Count the pads.' Variant by flag: allocated runner south, Overflow from 13, Sela's adult if letter-only, Fleet ashore if tender. Temperature. Then the game waits.

stages.text: Intercom. Cracked button. Tamsin states the temperature. A person on the apron wants a bunk the manifest provisioned. Manifest says fourteen. Count the pads.
Stool marks. Tracks. If Edor is also waiting, two waits that must not become a queue. Tamsin is not opening until you say. She is also not pretending they aren't there.
Let in (fifty walks inside), force decon (ten in the alcove), or deny (twenty off everyone who did not go out). The magnitudes are already written. Do not retune.
If in: Kess writes GUEST or a name, if they slept. Fourteenth row. The print was waiting. Or they are a pad. Pads are not rows.

choices.text: Let in. The tick walks inside. Fifty. Pads. A paper tag on a footboard that was not stencilled.
Force decon. Bucket. Rag. Ten in the alcove. They stand in the painted line and do not joke.
Deny. Twenty off everyone who did not go out. Tamsin keeps the wheel. Forty days. A ticket or a disc or a pair of hands in the ash.
Send to Allocation 11. Nila takes one. Not a column. One night. Two if the ice is wrong.

briefing: Someone has named Hadi Morrow who is not Hadi Morrow. Edor: 'Occupation observed: veterinarian. Stated: assistant. I can correct it.' The Quad strip wants a living trade. Pell needs a medic. Leva needs a whistle. Hadi: 'I can do this here with iodine and a clean rag. I can do the outfall with a whistle. I cannot do both in the same morning. You have to write which morning it is.'

stages.text: Hear the claim. Edor's form, the Quad strip, Pell's quota, or Leva's outfall. Someone has named Hadi who is not Hadi.
Talk to Hadi at the curtain. He will not self-name as doctor. He will pack a second rag if you say north. He will hate asking Nila.
List him, hide him, or send him. Kess writes veterinary assistant, observed. Or a blank where a trade was. Or a curtain on a wire with nothing behind it but a hook.
Optional: Ianov at the veterinary surgery. 'If he is gone, I do not round toward ease. I also do not grow a second pair of hands.'

choices.text: List him. Kess writes veterinary assistant, observed. Edor's form can be corrected. Cluster strip can come down. Levy can find him. Hadi: 'Put me on the morning row. Not the remarks.'
Hide him. Intercom lie check. Nila: 'If his name is already on a stool-form, I cannot unwrite it.' Kess leaves a blank where a trade was. She does not like the blank. She keeps it.
Send him. Kit: iodine, rag, warmth, welders' glass if Cut. Thirty days. Alcove curtain on a wire with nothing behind it but a hook.

briefing: Three names. They exist on more than one paper. If levy issued: Edor's carbon, pink in a satchel. If Pell: a ticket spike. If both: the same three bodies, two receipts. Kess lays the wall beside the carbon. Pencil or ink. Match or irregular. Tamsin: 'Route is Gate if the ice is a road. Weighbridge if Yara has gone dark.'

stages.text: Levy names vs morning row. Substitute is a status. Hide is a hatch in Overflow. Refuse is a stool.
Kit and route. Gate if the ice is a road. Weighbridge if Yara has gone dark.
Garrison high-vis over Cutter bone, or Pell alone with a receipt book. Service is the fastest route to rations. That is true.
Aftermath at the mess. Ladle protocol applies. Extra food looks like grief if you had a protocol. Looks like a pile if you didn't.

choices.text: Honour as written. Kit. Iodine. Glass. Column on the Cut or the Toll. Mess: two covered bowls.
Substitute. Kess: 'I can copy the wrong names. I won't misspell them. Irregular is the Office's word. I will still write what slept here.'
Refuse. In writing, or silence. Stool. Forty days. Lamps may go dark. Pell may arrive with a machine.
Hide at 11. Nila: 'One. Not three. Three is a column.' If you bring three she will take one and the other two are still a problem. Access is not a warehouse.

briefing: Filtration stack. Canisters. Behind them, the tin. Fourteen brass plates. Everyone who has found them has put them back. This time there is a buyer. Frayne's minutes want fittings. Leva's hall wants seats. The Quad chains have no seats. Your wall has names or does not. Kess is in the corridor. She does not comment on the tin. She never has.

stages.text: Open, or don't. Fourteen. Count living heads. Count fourteen. The extra plates are people who did not arrive. The missing plates, if any, are a quieter crime.
Keep it, sell north, sell to Works, or screw one plate under a living name. The tin is lighter by one. Nobody mentions it.

choices.text: Keep. Put it back. Hands know the way. Rectangles still unfaded.
North. Leva will not ask origin. Playground may still be chains.
Works. Mass, not origin. Water clock. Leva still short.
One plate on the wall. Screw a living name under a living name. Lamp-catch. The tin is lighter by one. Nobody mentions it.

briefing: The Archivists will not accept a living name on one testimony. Kess can be the second if she wrote the roster. Nila will not corroborate a name she is hiding. Completeness and blankness are the same fear, facing opposite ways. Boat if you must. Vault. Cotton gloves that are not yours.

stages.text: Copy the living list. Rubbing (pencil) or ink copy. Burning the chart before this fails the quest. Kess: 'I can say a name aloud. I wrote it. That is corroboration. It is not a religion.'

Margit Sole. She does not ask if it is fair. She asks if there is a second person who knew them. Two witnesses: she writes in a different ink. One: it cannot be made. The rule is the whole point of the rule.
Return. Kess asks what was said aloud. Say, whisper, or refuse.

choices.text: Two witnesses. She writes in a different ink. 'Say the name aloud while you write it. If you don't say it, you're only copying.'
One witness. 'Then it cannot be made. The rule is the whole point of the rule.'
Show 12-C if owned. She reads twice. She blots the date. She does not blot the refusal. She will still file living names if corroborated.

briefing: If the road is open: haulers leave; the house must hold. If the road is dark or Second Winter: everyone is home; steam may die north; arguments; illness; a visitor who cannot leave. Quest-first, not a weather DLC. Tamsin: 'Haulers out, house thin - or everyone in, stack a stack. Write the slate. I'm not a second stove.'

stages.text: Assign home watch vs waystation vs haul. Duty Roster: watch, mess, hatch, haul, waystation. Utility AI will default if you don't. Defaults are loud.
Survive N nights of shelter encounters. Night slate, meal, intake, hatch return, crowd. One per night unless crisis.
Resolve at least one returning-hatch dilemma with existing constants. Fifty. Ten. Twenty. Written.
Keep stove, filter, and child. Filter notches. A visitor who cannot leave.

choices.text: The house held. Night slate matches returns. Filter has notches you can count. Accident book empty, or honest.
Thinned. A name missing. Stove out at A, or filter death, or deny until the mess will not look at the wheel. Repeatable watches lock for a window.
Send Tamsin to Waystation A. Home grille is a grille. Cracked button louder. Steam watch gains a careful check.

briefing: The wall has waited, or it has been a morning row, or it has been a politics. Escorts read walls. Edor completes returns from walls. Nila closes wheels because of walls. Kess will not choose ink. 'Ink is a levy. I don't choose ink. I will write it if you order it. I will not pretend I chose it.'

stages.text: Hear Kess, Nila if access, Ansel, Tamsin. None of them will choose for you except Kess, who will not choose ink.
Ink, keep pencil, erase all, or burn. The wall is the document. The hatch reversed reads whatever remains.
Write the night slate, or don't. Tamsin: 'That's a different paper. I still need a wheel.'
Wait for the next hatch. Sela and/or Office escort. The wall is the document. The game gives you the temperature. Then it stops talking.

choices.text: Ink. Stick. Year-colour. Names that do not come off in the morning. Edor's return current. 11 dark if their living is included. Hatch reversed reads your list.
Pencil. Kess's preference. Audit risk. Nila still talks. Ice still wants a column.
Erase all. Wet thumb. Scars. Not a pool. Ormund incomplete. Stool may remain. Sole cannot complete what isn't written.
Burn. Kettle, or honesty. Header charred. Child asks. Fire in the kettle, or we did it, or silence.
